root_cause.verified: Packet publication previously crossed from the shared command runtime into a connection current-thread runtime. Tokio's external scheduling enqueues remotely and unparks the I/O driver; co-location uses its local task queue.
root_cause.source: Tokio 1.53.0 runtime/scheduler/current_thread/mod.rs:709-742 distinguishes local scheduling from remote queue plus driver.unpark. Its I/O driver calls mio 1.2.2 kqueue wake, issuing kevent on macOS.
root_cause.observed_chain: run_worker -> publish_batch -> BatchTransportState.submit/flush/send_group -> wake_by_val -> I/O driver Handle.unpark -> kevent
root_cause.profile_result: Across separately captured eight-client Time Profiler traces, the named send_group-kevent chain is 193ms sampled CPU in the predecessor and absent from the candidate's top-65 synchronization chains. Source confirms local publication. This is not proof that every remote wake or kevent disappeared.
root_cause.remaining: Shared cop-worker scheduler condition-variable waits/signals, SQL-to-worker rendezvous, direct reply parking and the asynchronous collector timer remain. They are not all explained by the removed publication hop. Complete critical-path attribution is still open.
rejected_hypotheses: Do not buffer unordered results to bypass Go's rendezvous: Go constructs that channel unbuffered.
Do not bypass real workers: Go EXPLAIN ANALYZE confirms four cop tasks for the tested range and the region inventory shows the actual four boundaries.
Do not treat active_attempts as stale terminal work: DirectUnaryQueryResponse removes a terminal attempt when accepting its response, before deciding on lite-worker fallback.
